new_jobs.description:
Description

Amazon Web Services (AWS) Infrastructure Security builds and operates the systems that protect customer data across the global data center fleet. The Raven team within Infrastructure Security owns the software and infrastructure that connects physical security devices to the network, provisions them, monitors their health, and manages their lifecycle — spanning cameras, intercoms, intrusion detection systems, and access control devices across hundreds of global data centers.

We are looking for a Technical Program Manager to drive the enablement of Zero-Touch Provisioning (ZTP) for physical security devices at scale. This TPM will own programs that directly accelerate data center build timelines by automating device onboarding and reducing manual intervention. The role covers three active program areas: Intercoms (cross-fabric deployment across global data centers), Perimeter Intrusion Detection Systems (infrastructure remediation and standardization), and the forward-looking roadmap for enabling additional physical security device types through our provisioning platform.

A critical component of this role is defining the physical security device requirements that enable new devices to be seamlessly integrated into our AWS data center security environment. The TPM will establish and maintain device integration standards — working with hardware vendors, firmware teams, and internal engineering to ensure that any device entering the fleet meets the connectivity, provisioning, and security requirements necessary for automated onboarding.

The TPM will work across hardware, software, and network teams to coordinate regional deployments, manage cross-team dependencies, and drive operational readiness for global device enablement. This individual will own program execution end-to-end — from requirements definition and stakeholder alignment through deployment and metrics-driven validation. They will partner closely with engineering to drive rollout schedules across global data centers and build mechanisms that scale provisioning without linear resource growth. The right candidate brings a data-oriented approach to prioritization, a bias for automation over manual process, and the ability to navigate ambiguity across hardware, firmware, and cloud infrastructure domains.

Key job responsibilities

The ideal candidate is customer obsessed, innovative, independent and results-oriented. As a Technical Program Manager, you will:

Define and own the physical security device integration requirements that enable new devices to be seamlessly provisioned into the AWS data center security environment through Zero-Touch Provisioning

Drive end-to-end program execution for Intercoms, Perimeter Intrusion Detection Systems, and the roadmap for future physical security device enablement across global data centers

Work with hardware vendors, firmware teams, and internal engineering to establish device connectivity, provisioning, and security standards that scale across the global fleet

Own deployment schedules and regional rollout coordination, managing cross-team dependencies across networking, security, and field operations to deliver against data center build timelines

Establish and manage operational metrics that measure provisioning adoption, deployment velocity, and device health — providing written and verbal updates to leadership

Collaborate with software development teams, network engineering, and data center operations to architect solutions that automate device onboarding and reduce manual intervention

Build mechanisms and processes that scale device enablement from individual sites to hundreds of global data centers without linear resource growth

Drive prioritization strategies using data to sequence device types, regions, and integration work against business impact and engineering capacity

Your job requires a high degree of judgment, the ability to negotiate and influence delivery across teams, comfort navigating ambiguity across hardware and software domains, and excellent communication skills.

About The Team

The Raven Team is part of Infrastructure Security at AWS. We build and operate software that automates physical security device lifecycle management across AWS data centers globally. Our platform — Skyward — handles automated device provisioning, health monitoring, and zero-touch onboarding for cameras, intercoms, intrusion detection systems, and access control devices. We work at the intersection of physical security and software engineering, partnering with security teams, data center operations, and hardware vendors. We're a small, high-ownership team solving real-world infrastructure problems at global scale.

3+ years of technical product or program management experience
2+ years of software development experience
3+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules

3+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience

At AWS, we're working to be the most customer-centric company on earth. To get there, we need exceptionally talented, driven people. Our Serviceability team owns serviceability excellence across AWS's global data center fleet. We set and maintain the preventive-maintenance (PM) standards, critical-spares strategy, and operational readiness testing programs for the electrical, controls, mechanical, and generator infrastructure that keeps AWS data centers online. We operate on a Global Process Owner (GPO) model: each Technical Program Manager owns a global program end-to-end — defining the maintenance standard, driving it through a gated review-and-approval lifecycle, and stewarding it globally across every AWS region. We turn field data into standardized, data-driven maintenance decisions that reduce risk, extend asset life, and lower cost at fleet scale.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we're the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we're looking for talented people who want to help.

You'll join a diverse team of infrastructure, software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. Develop, maintain, and continuously update integrated software project plans in Smartsheet, ensuring scope, milestones, dependencies, timelines, and overall status remain visible to engineering leadership and stakeholders.
Track day-to-day engineering activities, issues, and deliverables in GitLab, and translate relevant project-level status into JIRA for corporate visibility and cross-functional alignment.
Partner with Software Engineering leads to establish project execution priorities and continuously reassess plans based on technical progress, business needs, dependencies, and available resources.
Facilitate appropriate software development ceremonies and project reviews, including standups, sprint planning, backlog reviews, retrospectives, and milestone reviews, while maintaining alignment with the team's existing GitLab-based workflow.
Monitor project performance against commitments and drive corrective actions when schedule, scope, dependencies, or execution performance begins to deviate from plan.

Resource Allocation, Prioritization & Work Intake — 35%

Manage software engineering resource allocation across projects, ensuring engineers are appropriately assigned based on skills, priorities, workload, and project needs.
Establish and maintain a clear work-intake and prioritization process so that new software requests are deliberately evaluated before being assigned to the team.
Work with engineering leads to determine the highest-value activities for the team and ensure resources remain focused on agreed priorities.
Proactively identify when new projects or requests should be queued rather than immediately started, clearly communicating capacity limitations, priorities, and associated tradeoffs to leadership and stakeholders.
Support forward-looking capacity planning by identifying upcoming resource gaps, competing project demands, and potential staffing needs.

Cross-Functional Coordination, Risk & Stakeholder Communication — 25%

Coordinate software project activities across geographically distributed teams spanning multiple continents and time zones, maintaining alignment despite limited overlapping working hours.
Identify and surface project risks, technical blockers, dependencies, and resource conflicts early, and drive the appropriate owners toward resolution before delivery commitments are affected.
Maintain clear and consistent communication with Software Engineering leadership, Program Management, Systems Engineering, and other cross-functional stakeholders regarding project status, priorities, risks, and resource decisions.
Establish appropriate escalation paths for issues that cannot be resolved within the Software Engineering team.
Ensure project decisions, priorities, commitments, and changes are clearly documented and communicated across affected teams.
Provide concise project-level reporting to management, highlighting progress, upcoming milestones, major risks, resource constraints, decisions required, and recovery actions.

Proven ability to manage resource allocation and prioritization across teams supporting multiple concurrent projects and competing demands.
Demonstrated proficiency in tracking and communicating project status using structured planning and reporting tools such as Smartsheet, JIRA, or equivalent platforms.
Strong background partnering with software engineering teams and translating technical progress, risks, and schedule impacts into clear, actionable communication for leadership and non-technical stakeholders.

The Team

Role Summary

The Technology Compliance Program Manager Vulnerability Management is the sole subject matter expert in the technology compliance and vulnerability management domain. As an individual contributor, this role defines long-term strategy for the identification, assessment, prioritization, and remediation of security vulnerabilities across our technology environment and exercises considerable latitude and initiative to solve broad, complex problems.

Key Duties

As the lead subject matter expert in technology compliance, ensure the vulnerability management program aligns with regulatory requirements (e.g., PCI-DSS, HIPAA, NIST, ISO 27001) and integrates with other security tools such as SIEM, CMDB, and ticketing systems.
Define long-term strategy for developing, implementing, and continuously improving the enterprise vulnerability management strategy and roadmap.
Influence across company and several levels up to execute on IT assessments focusing on compliance with information security policy, procedures and standards.
Manage and optimize vulnerability management tools (e.g., Tenable, Qualys, Rapid7, etc.) to continuously improve the internal audit and risk management review.
Consult Alaska Air Group divisions, IT departments and project resources regarding the development, management approval, and implementation of objectives, goals, policies, standards, guidelines, and other requirement statements needed to support information security compliance throughout the company.
Serve as the primary point of contact between penetration testers and internal stakeholders, ensuring clear scope definition, rules of engagement, and minimal business disruption.
Define and track key performance indicators (KPIs) and metrics to measure program effectiveness.
Analyze and track findings, validate results, and work with relevant teams to prioritize and remediate identified vulnerabilities.
Manage execution of timely delivery of reports to leadership and stakeholders, maintain documentation, and integrate findings into the broader vulnerability management lifecycle.
Oversee regular vulnerability scanning and assessments across infrastructure, applications, and cloud environments.
Facilitate, schedule, and coordinate internal and third-party penetration tests across applications, networks, and cloud environments.
Maintain documentation and evidence for audits and compliance reviews.

Job-Specific Experience, Education & Skills

Required

7 years of experience in IT Security and Compliance, or related area.
Bachelor’s degree in Information Security, Information Technology, Computer Science or related field, or an additional two years of relevant training/experience in lieu of this degree.
Experience in project management, including all elements of scope, schedule, budgeting, risk evaluation, quality, integration, staffing, and communications.
Knowledge of security regulations (e.g., Sarbanes-Oxley, Payment Card Industry Data Security Specification [PCI DSS], Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act [HIPAA]) and standards (e.g. ISO 27001, NIST SP800-series).
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
High school diploma or equivalent.
Minimum age of 18.
Must be authorized to work in the U.S.

Preferred

Industry certification in security (e.g. CISA, CISSP, and/or GIAC).
Industry certification in project management (e.g. PMP).
2 years of experience leading people.
Demonstrated knowledge and experience in information security, software development and/or network security for large organizations.
Detailed technical knowledge in security engineering, system and network security, authentication and security protocols.

Job-Specific Leadership Expectations

Embody our values to own safety, do the right thing, be caring and kind, and deliver performance.
Create a culture where all employees feel safe and supported.

$141,250 - $211,900 / year

new_jobs.title: Security Program Manager, U.S. Amazon Dedicated Cloud
new_jobs.description:
Description

Amazon Web Services (AWS) Infrastructure Physical Security is seeking a highly talented and motivated Security Program Manager to join our team. AWS is the leading cloud provider, providing virtualized infrastructure, storage, networking, messaging, and many other services to customers all over the world to include the international public sector community.

The role is responsible for overseeing physical security design and the installation of security features and systems including access control, intrusion detection, camera surveillance, passive and active barriers, and other security features and capabilities consistent with AWS security standards and public sector contract requirements.

This role will perform security program management in support of new data centers, a logistics warehouse, data center expansions, and special security programs and projects.

You will be an individual contributor and will work directly with the Cluster Security Managers (CSMs), the Data Center Engineering Operations Team, and other customers, both internal and external, to integrate business and operations requirements into long-term physical security design and implementation. You will work with limited guidance to support the design and deployment of physical security packages and security program enhancements for AWS data centers and supporting facilities. Additionally, you will work across multiple teams and serve as the subject matter expert to author security design, security installation and sustainment contracts, and other security documents for submittal to the public sector customer. You will lead projects and develop short-term solutions in the physical security program. You may influence and manage vendor contracts to ensure industry-leading systems are deployed and sustained.

The ideal candidate for the role will be willing and able to work autonomously with minimal guidance or supervision, to build relationships across peer teams, stakeholders, and partner organizations, at all levels, and to be able to influence cooperation without authority in order to achieve program and project progress and completion. You will have an in-depth knowledge of electronic security and physical security system capabilities and leverage that expertise to make the right decisions for physical security projects, site sustainment, and deliver results on time and on budget. You are able to solve ambiguous problems, proactively identify existing or imminent security vulnerabilities, and apply mitigation strategies to reduce overall risk. You may be asked to use your knowledge to assess processes, program plans, and operations requirements to find security solutions or enhancements for routine and unique security requirements.

Additionally, the candidate will work across multiple teams within an Amazon Security organization to influence external customers, system owners, and business leaders. The candidate will effectively communicate with stakeholder audiences in a single domain and actively participate in meetings both internally and with the customer to drive business and technical discussions and decisions. This candidate will support their Manager in AWS external engagements with the customer. The role is based in the Phoenix, AZ area and will support multiple campuses and site types in the local cluster.

Key job responsibilities

Physical Security Design & Installation

Participate in physical security design for new data centers, data center expansions, logistics facilities, and special projects
Manage the installation of security features and systems including access control, intrusion detection, camera surveillance, passive and active barriers, and other capabilities consistent with AWS security standards and government requirements
Lead physical security team acceptance, sign-off, and operational readiness validation for high-security facilities in conjunction with other AWS teams
Apply knowledge of ICD 705 (Fixed Facility SCIF Construction), ICD Chapter 7 (Intrusion Detection), Chapter 8 (Access Control), Chapter 11 (Telecommunications Systems), and UL 2050 standards to security design and installation

Project & Budget Management

Provide physical security project lifecycle management including bid packages, specifications, drawings, code compliance, vendor management, budget tracking, change orders, and close-out documentation
Effectively and accurately manage multi-million dollar security project budgets — own and track the finance and budgeting process for assigned security programs and projects
Report performance metrics including vendor service delivery performance, actual spend vs. budget variance, cost reduction goal attainment, and post-installation defect rates
Manage purchase orders, invoice reconciliation, and financial accruals for security projects

Vendor & Contract Management

Manage vendor on-boarding, RFP/RFQ bidding, contracting, contract execution, QA/QC, and support processes for capital projects, preventative maintenance, and break/fix contracts
Influence and manage vendor contracts to ensure industry-leading systems are deployed and sustained
Monitor vendor performance against contract terms and delivery timelines; escalate underperformance through established channels
Coordinate with Procurement on new contract vehicles, renewals, and amendments
Manage preventative maintenance and break/fix contract execution to ensure security systems remain operational and compliant with accreditation standards

Security Program Support & Analysis

Support Cluster Security Managers by providing physical security analysis and recommending program enhancements to maximize security at assigned locations
Collaborate across teams to drive global, regional, and local security initiatives
Author security design documents, security installation and sustainment contracts, and other security documents for submittal to government customers
Provide physical security subject matter expertise on system capabilities, integration options, and compliance requirements

Stakeholder Engagement

Work directly with Cluster Security Managers, Data Center Engineering Operations, and government customers to integrate security requirements into facility design and operations
Serve as the physical security subject matter expert in cross-functional planning forums for new construction and facility expansion projects
Coordinate with government customer security representatives on physical security design approvals and accreditation requirements
Communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders regarding physical security standards and system designs

About The Team

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we are the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we are looking for talented people who want to help.

You will join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You will collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards of safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at our scale.

Diverse Experiences: AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn't followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don't let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS? Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world's most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that is why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture: Here at AWS, it's in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship & Career Growth: We are continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth's Best Employer. That's why you'll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance: We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there's nothing we can't achieve.

Basic Qualifications

5+ years of program or project management experience, or a Bachelor's degree and 5+ years of working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams experience
5+ years working with physical security design and/or implementation of electronic security systems such as access control, intrusion detection, and CCTV surveillance systems
Knowledge of MS Excel, AutoCAD, MS Project, Procore, BIM modeling tools, Bluebeam, AI assistants, and software for technical document writing such as Visio, Word, or PowerPoint
2+ years working in a regulated industry (government, banking, healthcare) where facility physical security requirements were audited and inspected
Must be a U.S. citizen with the ability to obtain and maintain a TS/SCI security clearance

Preferred Qualifications

Knowledge of ICD, NISPOM, NIST, and UL 2050 standards related to classified facility security, accreditation, and security system compliance
Project management or Physical Security certifications such as PMP, Scrum, or other Agile certification, or certification in Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design (CPTED), Certified Security Project Manager (CSPM), Physical Security Professional (PSP), or Security Project Management (SPM).
Experience with security-in-depth strategies and familiarity with convergence of physical and electronic security systems into integrated solutions and reading, interpreting, and creating construction drawings, specifications, and submittal documents
Bachelor's degree or above with experience in written and verbal communication skills to communicate with technical and non-technical audiences, including senior leadership
A U.S. citizen possessing an active TS/SCI security clearance

Through strong partnerships with Product, Data Science, Policy, Algorithm, ADSO-Search Operations, and front-line teams, we leverage diverse expertise to tackle safety challenges unique to user interactions.

With a commitment to data-driven improvement, we have developed a comprehensive metrics system to evaluate operational effectiveness, including moderation efficiency, quality metrics, and machine performance. By regularly monitoring and enhancing our processes, we work to exceed safety targets, close performance gaps, and continuously elevate the quality of platform interactions.

Our team also leads to building scalable, adaptable safety processes that meet both current and future needs. Through continuous process development, we ensure sustainable efficiencies and maintain operational excellence, evolving with the demands of a safe and thriving community.

About the role
- Operational Safety Management: Develop and implement a comprehensive framework for managing safety associated with Search, Comment and Messaging safety, with a strong focus on critical safety metrics including efficiency and quality metrics (e.g. CGVR, TCOA, and moderation/model performance). This includes setting up standards for key safety projects, workforce planning, enforcement mechanisms, and accuracy to ensure a cohesive and resilient safety strategy.
- End-to-End Process & Project Oversight: Oversee all stages of Search & Community Interaction Safety projects, ensuring that processes are designed to meet high standards of efficiency and quality. This includes preparing for projects meticulously and continuously monitoring key metrics to maintain and enhance operational excellence throughout each project's lifecycle.

Preferred Qualifications

Who is Litmus

Litmus is building the data foundation that powers industrial AI.

AI doesn’t work without real-world, contextualized data - Litmus makes that data usable. As AI adoption accelerates, most industrial environments still can’t access or use their operational data. We solve that gap.

We’re a growth-stage software company helping manufacturers access, structure, and use real-time data from machines, systems, and sensors at the edge. Our platform sits at the intersection of edge computing, AI, and industrial operations, enabling some of the world’s largest companies to run operations in real time, reduce downtime, and optimize production.

Backed by leading investors and trusted by global manufacturers and partners like Google, Microsoft, Dell, Oracle, and Mitsubishi, Litmus is powering the shift toward software-defined manufacturing.

Why join Litmus

Build the infrastructure that makes industrial AI possible

AI is moving beyond the cloud and into the physical world. At Litmus, you’ll build the infrastructure that enables real-time data to power AI and machine learning systems in production environments.

Work on problems where software meets the real world

Most AI systems fail without access to real-world data. You’ll build the layer that makes them viable in production. We solve challenges at the intersection of distributed systems, real-time data, and industrial constraints — where reliability, scale, and performance are non-negotiable.

Have real impact, fast

You’ll work on systems used by real customers in production, with direct impact on product and company trajectory. As a scaling company, we move quickly. You’ll have ownership, visibility, and the ability to shape both product and company as we scale.

Join a high-performance team

We’re building a team that holds a high bar and pushes each other to improve. You’ll work alongside experienced operators, engineers, and leaders who have done this before and are building again at scale. We hire people who take ownership, move quickly, and care about outcomes. No passengers.

Our culture

At Litmus, the team is collaborative, curious, and low ego. People are scrappy, take ownership, and look for ways to make an impact. We value empathy just as much as execution, whether that’s in how we build, how we communicate, or how we support each other.

We’re a growing company, so things move quickly and not everything is perfectly defined. If you enjoy figuring things out, working closely with others, and making steady progress, you’ll do well here.

NMI is looking for a highly analytical and data-obsessed Product Data Analyst
to help power decision-making across our acquiring operations and merchant lifecycle products. This role sits at the intersection of product, operations, and business intelligence — transforming large datasets into actionable insights that improve operational efficiency, merchant growth, product adoption, and financial performance.

You’ll partner closely with Product Managers, Operations, Engineering, Sales, Finance, and Support teams to deliver analytics and reporting across NMI’s acquiring ecosystem, including ISO management, Merchant Central, ScanX, business capital solutions, and other operational extensions.

This is an ideal role for someone who loves diving deep into data, building scalable reporting frameworks, uncovering trends and anomalies, and translating complex operational metrics into clear business insights. Strong SQL skills and a passion for data visualization through Tableau are essential.

If you thrive in fast-paced fintech environments and enjoy solving complex operational and product problems through data, we’d love to hear from you.

About NMI

NMI, a global leader in payment technologies, allows software and sales professionals to deliver payment innovations to their clients without having to build payment expertise in house. NMI enables our partners with choice, and challenges the one-size-fits-all approach to payments. You've probably used NMI in the last 24 hours without even realizing it. We're the platform that powers success for innovative tech created by SMBs, entrepreneurs and fintech startups. We're creative problem solvers who help visionaries smash through boundaries and think beyond what's possible so they can think about what's next. But we're not just built for the tech savvy. We democratize the latest payments technology so that everyone can realize the benefits of easy payments across the full spectrum of commerce. Our mission is to use our expertise to enable more payments, in more ways and more places. We provide ISOs, Fintech Innovators and Technologists the freedom to focus on what they do best, liberating them from restricted payment solutions and giving them access to the latest payment technology now and in the future.

How We Work - Our Core Values

Be a Good Person, It's Simple. We treat everyone fairly and with respect. We lead with kindness, humility and integrity. We take the time to understand each other and our customers. And we serve with care, because customers are never a transaction, and always our focus
Align, Trust & Go. We debate openly, listen carefully and challenge thoughtfully. Once we decide, we move forward together - holding ourselves accountable to our commitments, and focusing on what matters most to our customers. That alignment creates momentum.
Raise the Bar. Good enough isn't enough. We stay curious, measure everything, stay honest about progress and keep pushing ourselves to think creatively. We drive change, again and again. And leave things better than we found them. When we raise the bar, our customers feel it too.

Key Responsibilities

Product & Operational Analytics

Lead the collection, analysis, and interpretation of operational and product data to drive strategy, optimization, and growth across NMI’s acquiring platform and Merchant Central CRM
Partner closely with Product Managers supporting ISO operations, Merchant Central, ScanX, Business Capital lending, and additional acquiring extensions.
Build analytical frameworks that empower product and business teams to make data-driven decisions.
Conduct opportunity sizing, forecasting, trend analysis, and operational performance analysis to support strategic planning.

Dashboarding & Data Visualization

Design, build, and maintain Tableau dashboards and reporting frameworks that provide actionable visibility into KPIs, operational health, merchant performance, and product adoption.
Create executive-ready visualizations and narratives that clearly communicate insights to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Develop self-service reporting capabilities that enable teams to independently explore operational and product data.

Data Integrity & Operational Insights

Monitor data quality, transaction integrity, and operational reporting accuracy across the acquiring lifecycle.
Investigate anomalies, breakages, settlement discrepancies, reconciliation issues, and operational incidents proactively.
Analyze large transactional datasets to uncover trends, operational bottlenecks, growth opportunities, and merchant behavior insights.
Partner across teams to ensure accuracy in financial reporting, ACH reconciliation, settlement operations, and partner reporting.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Collaborate with Engineering and Data teams to define event tracking, instrumentation, and data collection standards.
Support business stakeholders across Product, Operations, Finance, Sales, and Support with timely insights and ad-hoc analysis.
Help establish KPI cadences and operational review processes across monthly, quarterly, and annual business rhythms.
Contribute to building a strong data discipline across product and operations teams through experimentation, measurement, and analytical rigor.

Process Improvement & Automation

Identify inefficient operational workflows and opportunities for automation through data and reporting improvements.
Help streamline operational reporting and reduce manual analysis through scalable analytics solutions and tooling.
Support experimentation frameworks, A/B testing analysis, and operational performance measurement initiatives.

Account Master Data Management & Modeling

Develop automated workflows to streamline account data maintenance, hierarchy updates, and data quality monitoring.

Data Engineering & Model Development

Design and build dimensional data models that support Sales reporting, analysis, and operational workflows across the organization.

Date Posted:
August 31, 2026

Space Dynamics Laboratory (SDL) is seeking an experienced Senior Cybersecurity Analyst
to join our corporate Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) team. This position will serve as a senior contributor responsible for leading the development and maintenance of cybersecurity documentation and policies, performing assessments, and managing continuous monitoring activities.

The successful candidate will help ensure SDL’s information systems remain aligned with applicable federal cybersecurity and contractual requirements, including NIST SP 800-171 and the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC). This role requires a strong understanding of cybersecurity risk and compliance, exceptional technical writing skills, and the ability to translate complex requirements into practical, risk-based actions.

This is an opportunity to take a leadership role in protecting information systems that support national defense, space exploration, and other mission-critical work.

Key Responsibilities

Governance, Policy, and Documentation

Leads the development, review, and maintenance of corporate cybersecurity policies, standards, procedures, plans, and supporting documentation
Ensures cybersecurity documentation accurately reflects implemented controls, organizational practices, contractual requirements, and current regulatory guidance
Leads the maintenance of System Security Plans (SSPs), Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), control implementation narratives, assessment records, and other compliance documentation
Establishes and maintains documentation governance practices, including document ownership, review cycles, version control, approvals, and evidence retention
Evaluates existing documentation for consistency, completeness, and audit readiness, and lead efforts to address identified gaps
Translates technical security implementations and federal requirements into clear, accurate, and defensible documentation

Assessments and Compliance

Leads internal security assessments, control validations, self-assessments, and compliance reviews against applicable requirements
Plans and coordinates assessment activities, including determining scope, identifying evidence requirements, interviewing control owners, validating assessment objectives, and documenting results
Supports organizational readiness for CMMC third-party assessments, government reviews, customer assessments, and other external compliance activities
Evaluates the design and implementation of security controls and determine whether available evidence adequately demonstrates compliance
Identifies compliance gaps, document findings, recommend corrective actions, and communicate results to technical teams and organizational leadership
Serves as a subject matter expert on NIST SP 800-171, CMMC, CUI protection requirements, and related federal cybersecurity frameworks

Continuous Monitoring and Risk Management

Leads continuous monitoring activities designed to verify that security controls remain implemented and effective over time
Develops and maintains continuous monitoring schedules, assessment plans, evidence requirements, and reporting mechanisms
Coordinates with control owners to gather, review, and maintain evidence and artifacts supporting ongoing compliance
Monitors changes to systems, technologies, threats, vulnerabilities, and regulatory requirements to determine their potential effect on organizational risk and compliance
Leads the tracking and management of identified deficiencies, POA&M items, remediation activities, and risk-based exceptions
Conducts cybersecurity risk assessments for information systems, business processes, third-party providers, and proposed technologies
Analyzes assessment and monitoring results to identify trends, recurring issues, and opportunities to improve the organization’s security and compliance posture
Prepares risk-based recommendations and clearly communicates material risks to technical and non-technical stakeholders

Organizational Collaboration and Advisory Support

Partners with information technology, engineering, legal, contracts, and business teams to integrate cybersecurity requirements into projects and operational processes
Provides senior-level GRC guidance during system implementations, architecture reviews, technology evaluations, and organizational change initiatives
Advises system owners and technical teams on security control requirements, documentation expectations, evidence sufficiency, and remediation strategies
Presents assessment results, compliance status, risks, and recommended actions to management and other stakeholders
Helps promote a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and risk-informed decision-making throughout the organization
Contributes to the development of security awareness and role-based compliance training materials

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree or higher in cybersecurity, information assurance, computer science, information systems, risk management, or a related field
Five to ten years of progressive cybersecurity experience, with substantial experience in governance, risk, and compliance
Demonstrated experience leading the development and maintenance of cybersecurity policies, standards, procedures, SSPs, POA&Ms, or comparable compliance documentation
Demonstrated experience planning or leading cybersecurity assessments, control testing, self-assessments, audits, or continuous monitoring activities
Strong working knowledge of NIST SP 800-171, CMMC, and the protection of Controlled Unclassified Information
Familiarity with related cybersecurity frameworks and standards, such as NIST SP 800-53, the NIST Risk Management Framework, or comparable federal requirements

Description

Senior Program Manager, Purchase – Retail Business Services

We are seeking a Senior Program Manager to lead strategy and execution for Shopping Mission Completion, ensuring customers can seamlessly discover, evaluate, and purchase products across the Amazon store.

About Amazon

Amazon.com, Inc. seeks to be Earth's most customer-centric company, where customers can find and discover anything they might want to buy online, and endeavors to offer its customers the widest of selection at low price that drives Amazon’s flywheel.

About The Team

The vision of Retail Business Services (RBS) Organization at Amazon is to accelerate Amazon’s flywheel by improving customer experience and enabling our Selling Partners (SPs) to grow their business with Amazon. RBS provides catalog augmentation and correction technologies for the Amazon selling community. Our solutions ensure information in Amazon's catalogs is both complete and comprehensive enough to give our customers a great shopping experience every time.

Role Overview

RBS is looking for a Senior Program Manager to lead a Strategy for Shopping Mission Completion for Customers. Amazon Store Walk analysis uncovers critical defects across the Amazon shopping journey; spanning across product discovery, evaluation, and purchase completion. These systemic problems impact the customer shopping journey, from how customers discover and evaluate products to their ability to complete purchases. These issues are categorized into four key defect themes: Data, Search, Catalog and Customer Experience. To resolve these issues, we recommend a coordinated, cross-functional engagement with partner teams that will improve overall customer shopping experience . This role will be at the center of collaboration between multiple world wide teams in re-imagining the purchase experience for customers.

Key job responsibilities

Shopping Mission is an essential part of the consumer experience and can fundamentally influence the way customers shop on Amazon as well as shape their perception of Amazon.

As a Senior Program Manager - Purchase, you will

Think Big and own vision for building a Strategy that enables customers to complete their shopping journey.
Disambiguate the problem space and size the problem and opportunity for RBS
Be responsible for end-to-end business strategy, goal setting, program management, review and collaboration mechanisms.
Break down ambiguous problems into clear abstract use cases and solution workflows for Tech and Product teams.
Be responsible for end to end program management with multiple parallel tasks.
Establish accountability with partner teams and influence them without authority on a common goals.
Identify risks and develop strategies to mitigate them.
Be responsible for reporting and review mechanisms and communication to Leadership (Flash updates, WBR, QBR, Deep dives)

To be successful in this role, you should be comfortable and confident liaising with remote global teams in business, design and technology at senior leadership levels. You will solve ambiguous problems and proactively identify and mitigate risks (before they become roadblocks). You will be data-driven and demonstrate good judgment in how and when to escalate (without damaging relationships).

Representing the voice of customers, you will be an evangelist for the program vision, maintaining support for your cause, keeping engineering teams energized and excited, and driving your program roadmap at all levels. You will be very comfortable with written communication skills and a proven track record of delivering projects from concept to launch.

About The Team

The 'Shopping Mission' program is part of the Customer Experience vertical of RBS. The program is responsible for defining the Vision and long term strategy of improving Customer Experience through improving the quality of Amazon products. RBS is the global sponsor of the program, bringing together multiple world-wide product, design and engineering teams to execute in a federated manner.

Basic Qualifications

5+ years of working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams experience
5+ years of program or project management experience
5+ years of delivering cross functional projects experience
Experience defining program requirements and using data and metrics to determine improvements

Preferred Qualifications

2+ years of driving process improvements experience
Master's degree, or MBA in business, operations, human resources, adult education, organizational development, instructional design or related field

new_jobs.title: Environmental Data Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

onsemi is seeking an Environmental Data Analyst to join the Energy & Sustainability Data Analytics team to support enterprise environmental data management and data-driven decision-making across global operations. This role will help collect, validate, reconcile, analyze, and report greenhouse gas (GHG), energy, water, waste, production, and related operational data while supporting issue resolution through internal and external systems.

The successful candidate will work closely with Operations, Industrial Engineering, Finance, Procurement, IT, and manufacturing sites to improve environmental data quality, maintain audit-ready documentation, resolve data gaps, and develop insights that support sustainability strategy, customer reporting, external disclosures, and operational improvement.

This position is ideal for a detail-oriented, analytical professional who is comfortable working with large datasets, collaborating across functions, and translating complex information into clear, actionable insights.

Responsibilities

Support enterprise GHG emissions inventory, accounting, forecasting, and reporting across Scope 1, Scope 2, categories.
Collect, validate, reconcile, and manage environmental data, including energy, water, waste, production, invoices, and other operational metrics.
Perform routine data quality checks, investigate missing invoices or incomplete records, and resolve environmental data gaps in partnership with site teams and subject matter experts.
Create and maintain Jira data entries, and related internal or external work tickets to track, escalate, and resolve data and system issues.
Prepare monthly and quarterly flux analyses to identify trends, anomalies, risks, savings, and opportunities across environmental and operational datasets.
Develop, maintain, and run reporting tables, dashboards, and analytics tools, including Tableau outputs for internal/external reporting.
Support development of Tableau dashboard, including table runs, data updates, user support, and training manual development.
Create spreadsheet templates and flat-file tools for internal use, and other recurring data collection or reporting needs.
Maintain Sharepoint and develop training manuals, process documentation, and user guidance to improve consistency and adoption.
Support IT project user acceptance testing (UAT), system enhancements, and data process improvements related to environmental data platforms, dashboards, and reporting tools.
Document best practices and standardized procedures to improve data quality, process consistency, and scalability across global sites.
Support product carbon footprint, lifecycle assessment, peer benchmarking, sustainability risk assessment, and other ad hoc sustainability initiatives.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Engineering, Data Science, Business, Economics, Sustainability, or a related field.
3–5 years of relevant experience in sustainability, environmental data management, ESG reporting, facilities, manufacturing, data analytics, or sustainability consulting.
Proficiency with data analysis, reporting, and visualization tools such as Microsoft Excel, Tableau and Power BI.
Experience working with large datasets, spreadsheet templates, data reconciliation, variance analysis, and recurring reporting processes.
Strong understanding of environmental metrics, including energy, water, waste, greenhouse gas emissions, invoices, production, and operational activity data.
Working knowledge of GHG accounting standards and sustainability reporting frameworks such as the GHG Protocol, CDP, GRI, SASB, TCFD, and EcoVadis.
Ability to evaluate data quality, identify gaps, investigate anomalies, maintain clear documentation, and support audit trails.
Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to explain findings, risks, and recommendations to technical and non-technical audiences.
Excellent organization and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, tickets, and recurring deliverables in a global, matrixed environment.
Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across functions, regions, and levels of the organization.
Comfort navigating ambiguity, evolving requirements, fast-paced business needs, and system/process changes.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in Environmental Science, Engineering, Sustainability, Data Science, Business, or a related field.
Experience in semiconductor, technology, manufacturing, or facilities environment.
Experience managing facility-level environmental data and supporting corporate sustainability reporting or assurance activities.
Experience with Tableau, Jira, SysAid, or similar dashboarding, environmental data management, ticketing, or workflow systems.
Experience building or improving environmental data processes, dashboards, forecasting tools, user guides, training manuals, or internal controls.
Strong attention to detail, intellectual curiosity, and ability to work proactively and independently.

About Us

onsemi
(Nasdaq: ON) is driving disruptive innovations to help build a better future. With a focus on automotive and industrial end-markets, the company is accelerating change in megatrends such as vehicle electrification and safety, sustainable energy grids, industrial automation, and 5G and cloud infrastructure. With a highly differentiated and innovative product portfolio, onsemi creates intelligent power and sensing technologies that solve the world’s most complex challenges and leads the way in creating a safer, cleaner, and smarter world.
